what_its_for: Vandetanib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid cancer that cannot be removed by surgery or has spread to other parts of the body. It works by blocking signals that tell cancer cells to grow and by cutting off the blood supply that feeds the tumor.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water, with or without food. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you cannot swallow the tablet whole, you may dissolve it in 2 ounces (about 60 mL) of non-carbonated water. Stir until the tablet is broken up (it may not fully dissolve) and drink it right away. Rinse the glass with more water and drink that too, so you get the full dose. Do not crush the tablet or dissolve it in other liquids.
dosing: The usual dose is 300 mg (one tablet) taken once a day. Your doctor may lower your dose to 200 mg or 100 mg if you have side effects or kidney problems. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and there are more than 12 hours until your next scheduled dose, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store vandetanib tablets at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them in the original bottle with the cap tightly closed. Store away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the amount of this drug in your body and worsen side effects. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds — this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so wear sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid taking antacids (like Maalox or Tums) at the same time as vandetanib; take them at least 2 hours before or after your dose. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially heart medicines, antibiotics, antifungals, or seizure medicines, because many drugs can interact with vandetanib. Women should avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine and for at least 4 months after stopping — it can harm an unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, fainting, or a fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat (this could be a serious heart rhythm problem); severe diarrhea, vomiting, or inability to drink fluids; sudden severe headache, confusion, vision changes, or seizures (signs of a rare but serious brain condition); skin blisters, peeling, or a severe rash; signs of bleeding such as coughing up blood, blood in your urine or stool, or unusual bruising; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; severe stomach pain; or any signs of infection such as fever or chills. Also call your doctor if you notice changes in your vision, persistent nausea, or any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Vandetanib does not cure cancer, but it can slow its growth and spread. It may take several weeks to months before your doctor can tell if the medicine is working, based on scans and blood tests. Many patients notice that their cancer stops growing or grows more slowly. Keep taking the medicine even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will adjust your dose if your kidneys are not working well. Liver problems: This medicine has not been fully studied in people with severe liver disease; your doctor will decide if it is safe for you. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age. Older adults (65 and older): No dose adjustment is needed based on age alone, but older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after your last dose.
